turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_constrained_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_constrained_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Both of these hard constraints apply to every candidate:
  1. molybdenum content at most 3.21 wt%;
  2. alloying cost index Σ (price_e × wt%_e) at most 450, using the prices in USD/kg: C 0.5, Mn 2, Si 2.2, Cr 9, Ni 17, Mo 25, V 30, Nb 45, Co 33, Al 2.4, Ti 12, Cu 9.
A candidate that violates either constraint is worth zero, so picking one wastes a slot. Using the training data, predict which FEASIBLE candidates have the HIGHEST yield strength (MPa), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Approach

**1. Feasibility screen (must pass both constraints)**

*Mo ≤ 3.21* eliminates c030 (3.58), c049 (3.73), c055 (3.22), c058 (3.67), c059 (4.55).

*Cost index ≤ 450* (Co, Ni, Cr, Mo, Nb, V dominate) eliminates many of the highest‑Co/highest‑Ni recipes, e.g.
c086 (627), c099 (≈460), c015 (469), c045 (472), c037 (451), c065 (464), c050, c020, c025, c032, c040, c077, c085, c098, c008, c072, c027, c036, c006 (475), c089, **and c057 (458 – very close, still over)**.

**2. What the training data says (group means, n≈300)**

| factor | evidence |
|---|---|
| **Co** | strongest positive driver: Co≈0 rows average ≈1500–1560; Co 6–9 rows average ≈1800–1900 (≈+45 MPa per wt%). All 10 highest targets (2010–2395) have Co 4–7 (or Ni≈9–12 + Mo). |
| **Ni** | positive up to ≈10–13 wt% (Ni 8–12 mean ≈1770 vs Ni<2 mean ≈1628), then **harmful** (Ni>14 mean ≈1581; Ni≈21 → 1256). |
| **Mo** | positive: Mo<0.2 mean 1568 vs Mo>2.5 mean 1728 (≈+55/wt%). |
| **aging_temp** | clear optimum ≈580–650 °C (mean 1762); 450–480 °C → 1611; >700 °C → 1560. |
| **heat_treatment** | quench_temper ≈+100, solution_aged ≈+20, quenched ≈+10, **annealed ≈−120**. |
| **route** | cast/wrought > AM (AM ≈−40). |
| C, Si, V, Nb, Al, Ti, Cr, solutionizing T, time, cooling | essentially neutral (Cr slightly negative above ~18 wt%). |

Fitting this simple additive form (Co, Mo, Ni‑with‑plateau, aging‑temperature parabola, HT and route offsets) reproduces the training extremes well (e.g. Co 6.25/Ni 3.2/Mo 1.4/quench‑temper → predicted 1989 vs measured 2019). A small extra penalty is applied when Co is high but Ni≈0, because such training rows (1520, 1562, 1596) fall short of the additive prediction.

**3. Scoring the feasible pool (top group)**

| cand | Co | Ni | Mo | aging | HT/route | pred (MPa) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| c092 | 6.75 | 1.8 | 2.60 | 552 | q_temper/AM | ~1940 |
| c044 | 4.72 | 6.49 | 0.95 | 660 | q_temper/cast | ~1925 |
| c007 | 5.26 | 10.24 | 0 | 685 | q_temper/wrought | ~1910 |
| c042 | 3.34 | 9.69 | 2.36 | 509 | sol_aged/cast | ~1870 |
| c003 | 4.38 | 7.51 | 0 | 526 | q_temper/cast | ~1855 |
| c051 | 3.43 | 13.2 | 0.06 | 695 | q_temper/cast | ~1855 |
| c029 | 4.86 | 9.04 | 0.66 | 661 | quenched/wrought | ~1850 |
| c075 | 5.93 | 0 | 1.18 | 616 | q_temper/cast | ~1847 |

All five selections satisfy Mo ≤ 3.21 and cost ≈ 335–435 (< 450).

**Final: c092, c044, c007, c042, c003**
